source.title: Equivariant bifurcation, quadratic equivariants, and symmetry breaking for the standard representation of S k

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied; no apparent cutoff or garbling that prevents reading relevant sections.
record.tranche_reason: The paper reports a numerical/analytic study of a shallow student-teacher ReLU model's spurious minima and analyzes a bifurcation mechanism, conceptually bearing on whether gradient dynamics encounter spurious minima. It does not reproduce the versions' benchmark training-error claims; its main contribution is a mathematical bifurcation analysis.
record.gate_note: The paper's mathematical bifurcation theorems concern generic equivariant vector fields, not measured training classification error. Its neural-network section reports numerical Hessian/bifurcation findings for type II critical points, which bear on the broader spurious-minima subject but not the specified training-error, initialization, depth, width, learning-rate, or normalization behaviors. Cited benchmark results and claims are not recorded as this study's own results.
record.test_reason: The study analyzes how spurious minima form through equivariant bifurcation. It does not measure V2's gradient-descent endpoint frequencies as teacher and student grow, or compare matched widths with extra student neurons. Critical-point stability and bifurcation geometry do not establish those training behaviors. No other version is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: The record is broadly accurate. The authors develop generic equivariant bifurcation theory and minimal models of forced symmetry breaking to explain the creation of spurious minima through local landscape deformation rather than bifurcation of global minima. Their application to type II neural-network minima combines earlier Hessian results with numerical checking; a general mechanism across families remains conjectural.
record.recipe_differences: The neural-network discussion is a mathematical and numerical bifurcation analysis of a shallow ReLU student-teacher loss; it does not test the listed training recipes or training-error claims.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported critical-point stability changes with neuron count: the type II point is a saddle for k ≤ 5 and a local minimum for k ≥ 6; the Hessian bifurcation is estimated near k ≈ 5.58.

fits_no_version.finding: Section 5 reports numerical checking that type II critical points undergo bifurcations along symmetry axes near k ≈ 5.58. The saddle-to-minimum transition between k ≤ 5 and k ≥ 6 and its Hessian analysis are attributed to earlier work.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In the symmetric, matched-width ReLU student-teacher loss, type II spurious minima form through a bifurcation involving the standard representation.

fits_no_version.finding: Theorems 4.4 and 4.28 construct minimal symmetry-breaking models and establish counts of saddle-node bifurcations and crossing curves.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Local creation or annihilation of spurious minima can require complex landscape deformation under symmetry breaking.

record.problems: The neural-network discussion describes numerical checking and Hessian analysis without reporting sample sizes, optimizer details, uncertainty estimates, or a complete account of the numerical procedure in this paper. The central bifurcation results are theoretical and do not measure training classification error.
record.rows_left_out: No qualifying rows: the paper's result relevant to spurious minima is a qualitative/quantitative critical-point stability discussion, which is outside every listed version's specified measure. Cited results and theoretical bifurcation statements are not separate measured outcomes for those versions.

untested.parts: Training classification error on CIFAR-10/100, including random labels and model-size or training-recipe comparisons.
Frequency of convergence to spurious minima from standard initialization as teacher and student grow together; reduction with one or two extra student neurons.
Training degradation with depth and its prevention by identity shortcuts or special initialization.
Effects of initialization on training speed, signal propagation and trainable depth.
Learning-rate-dependent loss recovery, divergence and sharpness trajectories around the stability threshold.
Training speed and learning-rate tolerance with batch normalization or Fixup.

record.verdict_notes: The record's tests/T2 classification conflicts with its own gate note and should be replaced by discusses/T6. Empty rows and verdicts are appropriate. E1's first locator should be Section 4, page 27, rather than Section 1.2, page 4. Section 5, page 54 contains the conjecture paraphrased in E3.

versions.untested_parts: CIFAR training error, corrupted or random labels, model size, optimizer, initialization, and training duration are not tested.
No teacher-student width sweep or gradient-descent endpoint frequency is tested; the shallow-network numerical discussion concerns critical-point stability as neuron count changes.
No plain-versus-residual depth or training-error comparison.
No initialization comparison or trainable-depth experiment.
No learning-rate stability or loss/curvature trajectory experiment.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
